chunks: And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who marries a woman and stipulates upon her that he will visit her whenever he wishes and provide for her a specified amount, he said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm/it is valid

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling if a husband stipulates in the marriage contract that he will visit his wife whenever he chooses?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a stipulation allowing the husband to determine the timing of conjugal relations, reflecting the flexibility of Shia contract law in balancing mutual rights. This ruling underscores that such conditions do not invalidate the marriage (*nikah*) but rather define the practical execution of marital duties, a key topic in the chapter on dowry and marriage stipulations. It highlights the scholarly view that specific temporal conditions are permissible as long as they do not contradict the essential nature of marriage.
